subject.title: [Feature]: Intent-scoped MCP activation for large MCP catalogs

question: Should existing `toolsAllow` planning become the source of truth for per-run MCP activation, or should OpenClaw expose a separate request-scoped server-selection API?
rationale: The performance gap is concrete, but the permanent API, precedence rules, and ownership across tool policy, catalog caching, and direct operations require maintainer intent.

options.title: Tool policy owns activation
options.body: Carry a normalized full, none, or named-server activation plan from existing run tool policy into catalog materialization and direct target operations.

options.title: Add a separate selector
options.body: Introduce a new server-selection input with explicit precedence and conflict semantics against `toolsAllow`.

options.title: Keep full activation
options.body: Retain all-server catalog semantics and continue improving only concurrency and runtime reuse.

recommendation.title: Tool policy owns activation
recommendation.body: Carry a normalized full, none, or named-server activation plan from existing run tool policy into catalog materialization and direct target operations.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision most directly affects the canonical embedded-run tool-policy planning surface recently maintained by this contributor, with MCP runtime input needed from the other listed owners.
